News | September 15, 2026 Samsung Biologics Signs USD 262 Million Manufacturing Agreement With European Pharmaceutical Company Source: Samsung Biologics Agreement The agreement was disclosed in accordance with Korean market disclosure requirements. The new USD 262 million manufacturing agreement with a European pharmaceutical company reflects sustained client demand, with manufacturing commitments extending through 2033. Production under the agreement will take place at Samsung Biologics’ Songdo manufacturing site in South Korea. Capacity across Samsung Biologics’ existing manufacturing network continues to be reserved rapidly amid strong long-term manufacturing demand, underscoring robust utilization and continued business momentum. Samsung Biologics’ cumulative contract value surpasses USD 21.9 billion following the latest agreement. The client’s name and product-specific details will remain confidential under the terms of the agreement. Business momentum & long-term growth The latest agreement comes as Samsung Biologics continues to secure long-term client commitments, with available manufacturing capacity being filled quickly as the company advances its growth strategy across capacity, portfolio, and geographic expansion. Expanding the global network and capacity: Samsung Biologics operates 845 kL of manufacturing capacity across Korea and the U.S., comprising 785 kL in Songdo and 60 kL at its Rockville, Maryland, site. The Rockville site, acquired in March 2026, established Samsung Biologics’ first U.S. manufacturing presence, further diversifying the company’s global manufacturing network. The company has built a regional support network with offices in New Jersey, Boston, Tokyo, and Amsterdam, providing closer proximity to clients across the U.S., Europe, and Japan. Samsung Biologics has also secured land for Bio Campus III, laying the foundation for its next phase of long-term capacity and capability expansion, with plans to support dedicated R&D and manufacturing programs for next-generation therapeutics. The company continues to evaluate future capacity investments in line with long-term market demand and evolving client needs. Broadening the portfolio: Samsung Biologics has announced an all-cash offer to acquire PolyPeptide Group, with the proposed acquisition expected to expand its capabilities into peptide-based therapeutics and further diversify its global network. The proposed acquisition represents a key step in broadening Samsung Biologics’ portfolio beyond its established biologics capabilities to address a wider range of modalities and client needs. Samsung Biologics continues to expand its capabilities across monoclonal antibodies, bioconjugation, mRNA, organoid-based services, and next-generation development platforms, supporting increasingly diverse client pipelines. Investing behind the long-term growth strategy: Samsung Biologics announced a KRW 3 trillion rights offering in August 2026 to support strategic investments across its long-term growth strategy of capacity, portfolio, and geographic expansion. Approximately KRW 2.71 trillion is planned for the proposed PolyPeptide Group acquisition, with approximately KRW 290 billion designated for the expansion of Bio Campus II. About Samsung Biologics Samsung Biologics (KRX: 207940.KS) is a leading contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO), offering end-to-end integrated services that range from late discovery to commercial manufacturing. With a combined biomanufacturing capacity of 785,000 liters across Bio Campus I and II in Korea, and 60,000 liters at its manufacturing facility in Rockville, Maryland, U.S., Samsung Biologics holds a total global manufacturing capacity of 845,000 liters. Samsung Biologics has also secured land for Bio Campus III, laying the groundwork for future capacity expansion to support next-generation therapies and emerging modalities. Samsung Biologics leverages cutting-edge technologies and expertise to advance diverse modalities, including multispecific antibodies, fusion proteins, antibody-drug conjugates, and mRNA therapeutics. By implementing the ExellenS™ framework across its manufacturing network with standardized designs, unified processes, and advanced digitalization, Samsung Biologics ensures plant equivalency and speed for manufacturing continuity. Samsung Biologics' global manufacturing and commercial network spans Korea, the U.S., Europe, and Japan. Samsung Biologics America supports clients based in the U.S. and Europe, while its Tokyo sales office serves the APAC region. Samsung Biologics continues to invest in new capabilities to maximize operational and quality excellence, ensuring flexibility and agility for clients. Samsung Biologics is committed to the on-time, in-full delivery of safe, high-quality biomedicines, as well as to making sustainable business decisions for the betterment of society and global health. Article | September 11, 2026 Chromatography Polishing Under Pressure: New Demands Source: Cytiva By Henrik Ihre, Ph.D., Distinguished Fellow at Cytiva Platform monoclonal antibody processes were designed for a different era. As upstream titers climb and the range of antibody formats expands, the assumptions embedded in conventional polishing strategies are under pressure. Impurity profiles are more complex, structural diversity is greater, and the margin for error in process design is narrowing. In a panel discussion, Cytiva scientists Eva Heldin, Niklas Jungnelius, and Jakob Liderfelt examine what this shift means for chromatography polishing specifically: why it is becoming a more consequential point of differentiation in process design, how productivity and process economy factor into polishing decisions, and where current approaches may fall short.
